title: Containment-to-Stabilization Flow and Selective Backport Guidelines
creator: Liam Chen
description: Purpose: define a concise, operator-friendly flow that takes an incident from initial containment through a safe stabilization (hotfix) and selective backporting to LTS branches. This ticket codifies severity thresholds, branch naming and patch strategy, gating for canary and global rollouts, and automation hooks to reduce human error. The goal is to shorten time-to-safe-state without over-propagating risky changes to LTS. Scope excludes postmortem writeups and capacity scaling work - those are separate follow-ups.
problem_statement: When urgent regressions occur in production, teams need a predictable containment path that reduces blast radius quickly and a clear rule set for which 1) fixes must be backported to LTS and 2) which fixes can remain in the next minor release only. Current decisions are ad hoc and delay mitigation or cause unnecessary LTS churn.
severity_matrix:
Severity Criteria (summary):
- Sev 0 (P0-critical): production loss for >5% customers or data corruption; requires immediate hotfix lane.
- Sev 1 (P0-high): significant feature-wide failure impacting many users or violating SLAs; urgent hotfix evaluation.
- Sev 2 (P1-medium): degraded performance or partial failures; prefer patch in next minor unless reproducible regression on LTS workloads.
- Sev 3 (P2-low): cosmetic or minor issues; deferred to regular release cadence.
Decision rule: Any bug causing data loss or backward-incompatible behavior on LTS => mandatory backport. Performance regressions with >=20% latency amplification on LTS workloads => backport candidate after QA signoff.
containment_steps:
Containment runbook (operators):
1) Triage: assign on-call triage lead and set severity.
2) Scope: determine affected services, endpoints, and LTS/minor release exposure.
3) Quick mitigation: apply config toggles, feature flags, or traffic steering (region/model fallbacks).
4) Hotfix lane: create hotfix branch (hotfix/<ticket>-YYYYMMDD) off the exact release commit; open minimal PR with changelog entry and rollout plan.
5) Canary: deploy to 1% traffic, monitor the rollout dashboard and key SLOs for 30 minutes.
6) Rollforward or rollback rules: if error rate or latency exceed thresholds for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets, trigger automated rollback and escalate to incident commander.
7) Stabilize: once canary is green for the defined window, increase to 10% then 50% before full rollout.
8) Post-deploy: capture root cause and indicate backport decision within 24 hours.
branching_and_backport_policy:
Branch policy:
- Hotfix branches: hotfix/ENG-<id>-<summary>-<date> created from release tag.
- Patch commits must be single-purpose and include test updates and a short rationale.
- Dual-commit strategy: land hotfix to release branch and backport PR(s) to LTS branches when required. LTS branch names: lts/<major>.<minor>-stable (e.g., lts/1.18-stable).
Backport rules:
- Mandatory backport: data-loss, security, critical compatibility regressions.
- Conditional backport: performance regressions, availability issues — requires release engineering + product signoff.
- Not backported: UI/UX copy, experimental features, non-customer-facing telemetry changes.
Automation: use scripts in repo tools/release/backport.sh to create cherry-pick PRs and run the backport CI pipeline that enforces changelog and test coverage.
gating_and_rollout_controls:
Gates and signals:
- Canary thresholds (configurable per-service): error_rate > 0.5% OR p95 latency increase > 20% => fail.
- Automated canary rollback: deployment controller will roll back to previous stable if fail conditions persist for 3 checks.
- Manual abort: SRE or incident commander can abort rollout with reason logged.
- Rollout windows: avoid >75% rollouts during scheduled maintenance windows; prefer 03:00–08:00 UTC for infra-affecting fixes.
- Telemetry: must include a minimal set of metrics in the PR description: error rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and token throughput for the affected model serving surface.
qa_and_signoff:
QA signoff checklist:
- Repro steps documented and unit/integration tests added.
- Canary acceptance: no regressions in automated smoke tests and performance job (workload-sim) passes within 10% of baseline.
- Security: confirm no credential or KMS changes except via separate key rotation flow.
- Product: product manager confirms customer impact classification and approves backport if required.
- Release Engineering: validates branch origin and that backport CI is green.
rollback_criteria:
Rollback triggers (examples):
- Correctness: functional errors causing incorrect responses or data mutations.
- SLA breach: error rate or latency consistently above gates for 3 observation windows.
- Downstream impact: causes upstream services to cascade into other critical workflows.
Rollback steps: revert PR using the release controller, redeploy previous artifact, and mark the hotfix PR as reverted with a follow-up action. Post-rollback, capture timeline and take an emergency code freeze for the affected component until RCA is drafted.
automation_and_tools:
Planned tooling updates:
- backport.sh enhancements to create PRs against multiple LTS targets with a single command and to auto-fill changelog entries.
- Release controller improvements to allow parameterized canary windows and auto-rollback on composite signals.
- Dashboard: add per-hotfix panes showing canary windows, rollback history, and backport status to Console (release-tech section).
- CI guard: introduce a pre-merge check that rejects hotfix PRs missing the canary rollout plan or required test artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runbook drafted and validated by SRE and Release Engineering.
- backport.sh updated with at least one dry-run against lts/1.18-stable and documented in the repo README.
- New hotfix branch naming enforced by commit hook.
- At least one simulated hotfix scenario executed in staging with automated rollback triggered and documented.
